items.front: Capital of the Kakatiyas (and earlier seat)?
The Kakatiyas rose to sovereignty from feudatories of which power?
items.back: The Western (Kalyani) Chalukyas (earlier also under the Rashtrakutas); independent under Rudradeva/Prataparudra I (1163).

items.front: Who built the Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda, and issued the Anumakonda inscription (1163)?
Greatest Kakatiya ruler (r.1199–1262); issued which trade charter?
items.back: Ganapati Deva; the Motupalli Abhaya-shasanam protecting overseas merchants.

items.front: Kakatiya woman sovereign, and the traveller who described her realm ('Mutfili')?
items.back: Rudrama Devi (r.c.1262–1289); described by Marco Polo.

items.front: Last Kakatiya ruler, and the year Warangal finally fell?
items.back: Prataparudra II; fell in 1323 CE to Ulugh Khan (Delhi Sultanate); Orugallu renamed Sultanpur.

items.front: Ramappa (Rudreshwara) Temple — location, builder, distinctive engineering?
items.back: Palampet (Warangal); built 1213 by Recherla Rudra; 'floating'/sandbox foundation & light spongy bricks.

items.front: When did the Ramappa Temple become a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
items.back: 2021 (44th session) — the only temple in India named after its sculptor, Ramappa.
A chain of irrigation tanks — Pakhal, Laknavaram and Ramappa lakes (tank-based farming).

items.front: Kakatiya land-for-service military system (later borrowed by Vijayanagara)?
items.back: The Nayankara system — assigning land to Nayakas for military service; enabled peasant-warrior social mobility.

items.front: Iconic Kakatiya gateway that is the Telangana state emblem?
items.back: The Kakatiya Kala Thoranam (Warangal Fort kirti-toranas); dynasty's clan goddess was Kakati (Durga).

items.front: Which lineage recovered Warangal after the Kakatiya fall?
items.back: The Musunuri Nayakas — Prolaya Nayaka (Vilasa grant, 1330) and Kapaya Nayaka (recovered Warangal 1336).

items.front: Notable Telugu literary patronage in the Kakatiya age?
items.back: Palkuriki Somanatha and Tikkana; Jayapa Senani's dance treatise Nrittaratnavali.

items.front: Sieges of Warangal before its 1323 fall?
items.back: 1310 (Malik Kafur), 1318, and 1323 (Ulugh Khan) — Prataparudra II finally defeated in 1323.
